 Best known for his role as Dean Winchester, Jensen Ackles has seemingly left his role in Supernatural behind and is starring in big projects like The Boys and Tracker . Ackles made his debut as Soldier Boy in Season 3 of the Prime Video series, and after going on hiatus for most of Season 4, he returned to prominence in the fifth and final season earlier this year, but the franchise isn’t done with him yet. Ackles, alongside Aya Cash , has been tapped to star in the second Boys spin-off show, Vought Rising , which is coming to Prime Video sometime in 2027. Last year, Ackles was also recruited to lead a new crime drama co-starring the late Eric Dane , Countdown , but the show was canceled after only one season.

 Despite all these new roles, it will be hard for anything Ackles does in the future to top his work in Supernatural — he played Dean Winchester for an impressive 15 seasons and 20 years. The story of Supernatural on-screen may have come to an end back in 2020, but the franchise has continued with the new comic series, Supernatural: Sam Winchester #1 , which hit shelves earlier this month on October 7. The new run is set at an undisclosed time during the earlier seasons of the show, and it follows Sam in Appalachia where he encounters Eldritch-type horrors. However, despite his long run on the show, Ackles’ co-star Jared Padalecki is not involved with the new comic at all, aside from the use of his likeness and a photograph for one of the variant covers. Ackles was also left out of Supernatural: Dean Winchester #1 earlier this year, aside from his physical likeness. Issue #2 will continue Sam's story on November 4, 2026.

 Collider Exclusive · 8 Questions · 2 Minutes 
 What Fantasy World Do You Belong To? 
 Middle-earth · Grand Line · The Continent · Camp Half-Blood 
 Pick your magic, your crew, where you want to wake up and who you would rather be fighting, and we will tell you which world you actually belong in. Four are open to you: an ancient kingdom living through its last good age, an endless sea full of pirates, a continent that pays people to kill monsters, and a summer camp where the Greek gods are extremely real and mostly a nuisance. 
 💍 Middle-earth (Rings of Power) 
 👒 Grand Line (One Piece) 
 🐺 The Continent (The Witcher) 
 🔱 Camp Half-Blood (Percy Jackson) 
 FIND YOUR WORLD → 
 QUESTION 1 / 8 THE POWER 
 01 
 What kind of power do you want? 
 Every one of these worlds runs on a completely different sort of magic. 
 A Something ancient and half forgotten that came down through my family. 
 B Something completely ridiculous that works in a fight and gets a laugh. 
 C No magic at all, just training, potions and a very sharp sword. 
 D Something I inherited from a parent I have barely met. 
 NEXT QUESTION → 
 QUESTION 2 / 8 THE COMPANY 
 02 
 Who is travelling with you? 
 Nobody gets through any of these stories entirely on their own. 
 A A fellowship drawn from every corner of the world who barely trust each other. 
 B A crew I picked up one at a time, all of whom would die for me. 
 C Two or three people I would never describe out loud as friends. 
 D Two mates from school who are exactly as out of their depth as I am. 
 NEXT QUESTION → 
 QUESTION 3 / 8 THE HOME 
 03 
 Where do you want to wake up tomorrow? 
 The best fantasy is usually just somewhere you would genuinely like to live. 
 A A high city of white stone with the sea somewhere far below. 
 B A ship under sail, with an island ahead that nobody has mapped. 
 C A rented room over a tavern, in a town I am leaving in the morning. 
 D A cabin at a summer camp with everybody else already awake outside. 
 NEXT QUESTION → 
 QUESTION 4 / 8 THE LIVING 
 04 
 How are you making a living out there? 
 Even in fantasy somebody has to pay for the horse. 
 A I am not, because somebody far older than me decided this was my duty. 
 B Treasure, and I am not always careful about whose it used to be. 
 C I take contracts, since people will pay well for what they will not touch. 
 D I am fifteen and this is all technically a school trip. 
 NEXT QUESTION → 
 QUESTION 5 / 8 THE MONSTER 
 05 
 There is something in the woods. What do you do about it? 
 All four of these worlds keep something unpleasant out there in the dark. 
 A Send word to somebody who has seen this before, then hold the line. 
 B Walk straight in, because it is interesting and possibly edible. 
 C Ask what it has been eating and what the village is willing to pay. 
 D Work out which myth it escaped from, then improvise very badly. 
 NEXT QUESTION → 
 QUESTION 6 / 8 THE ENEMY 
 06 
 Who is the villain of your story? 
 The enemy tells you far more about a world than the hero ever does. 
 A An ancient evil that has been patient for several thousand years. 
 B A government that has spent a long time calling itself the good guys. 
 C A man who turns out to be far worse than anything I hunt for money. 
 D A god, or possibly my own family, and quite likely both at once. 
 NEXT QUESTION → 
 QUESTION 7 / 8 THE CREED 
 07 
 What do you actually believe in out there? 
 Every world hands its heroes one rule and asks them to hold onto it. 
 A Some things are worth defending even when the odds are hopeless. 
 B Nobody gets to tell me where I can go or what I am allowed to want. 
 C Pick the lesser evil, and never pretend afterwards that it was not evil. 
 D My friends come before anything a prophecy has to say about it. 
 NEXT QUESTION → 
 QUESTION 8 / 8 THE LEGEND 
 08 
 A thousand years from now, how are you remembered? 
 Eight questions in, this is the one that decides your world. 
 A In a song, in a language hardly anybody still speaks. 
 B As the one who got there first and proved the whole thing was possible. 
 C Barely, and mostly wrongly, in ballads I would absolutely hate. 
 D On a plaque at a camp, read by kids about to do the same thing. 
 REVEAL MY WORLD → 
 The Map Is Drawn 
 Your World Is… 
 Four worlds and four completely different ideas of what a good life
 looks like. This is where you belong, what it would ask of you, and what you would get back in
 return.
 The Rings of Power · Prime Video · Since 2022 
 Middle-earth 
 You belong somewhere old enough that the mountains have names and
 somebody can still tell you who gave them. Middle-earth is for people who think the right
 thing is worth doing even when it will not be finished in their lifetime.
 This is the only world on the list where doing good is understood as a very long defeat,
 fought anyway, by people who will never see how it ends.
 You are drawn to grandeur, to white cities and deep forges and the sense that almost
 everything you touch is older than your entire family line.
 The Rings of Power is set in the last good age before it all goes wrong, which gives
 every quiet scene in it a slightly unbearable weight.
 You would take the hard road, and you would take it on foot.
 One Piece · Manga since 1997 · Netflix 2023 
 The Grand Line 
 You want the sea, a crew, and absolutely nobody telling you where
 you are allowed to go. The Grand Line is the world for people whose main ambition in life is
 finding out what is over there.
 One Piece has run for decades on one very simple engine, which is a group of people who
 each want something impossible and have decided to go and get it together.
 You collect people. Your ideal crew is a set of misfits who were each written off
 somewhere else before you turned up and offered them a better idea.
 The world is enormous and deliberately ridiculous, and the emotional gut punches land
 harder because of that rather than in spite of it.
 You would set sail knowing the map runs out, which is more or less the entire point of
 it.
 The Witcher · Netflix · Since 2019 
 The Continent 
 You would rather be feared and useful than liked and useless. The
 Continent is a world where the monsters are the straightforward part of the job and the
 people are where it all gets complicated.
 Witchers get paid to do what nobody else will and resented for existing at all, which is
 a trade most people would refuse and you would probably accept.
 You have no real illusions about which side is the good one, largely because on the
 Continent that question tends to have a disappointing answer.
 The best of these stories are not about the fighting. They are about somebody with a
 rigid code being repeatedly cornered into caring about people.
 You would take the coin, finish the job properly, and be out of town before the story
 got told wrong.
 Percy Jackson · Disney+ · Since 2023 
 Camp Half-Blood 
 You want the myths to be real and loose in the actual world, and
 you want to find out at about thirteen that you were never anywhere near as ordinary as
 everybody kept telling you.
 Percy Jackson takes the oldest stories we have and drops them into car parks and diners,
 which makes the gods considerably funnier and a great deal worse.
 You would be the kid every school gave up on, who turns out to have been built for
 something nobody thought to test for.
 The series is genuinely about friendship rather than destiny, and it says so out loud
 every time a prophecy tries to get in the way.
 Camp Half-Blood is the real fantasy here: a place where the thing that made you
 difficult everywhere else is the thing that makes you belong.
 ↻ RETAKE THE QUIZ 
 Here’s How To Watch All 15 Seasons of ‘Supernatural’ on Streaming
 All 15 seasons of Supernatural are streaming on both Prime Video and Peacock, and neither platform has announced plans for the show to depart streaming anytime soon. Supernatural used to also stream on Netflix , but the show left the platform last year before migrating to its new homes. There have been whispers for years about a Supernatural reboot, but most fans agree that not enough time has passed for a potential reimagining to effectively capture the nostalgia it would need to get off the ground.
 Check out all 15 seasons of Supernatural on either Prime Video or Peacock and stay tuned to Collider for more updates and coverage of Jensen Ackles’ future projects.
